publicly_readable: The launch press release (2017-11-20), which lists twelve global themes, and the editor's introduction in full (worldin.economist.com, Internet Archive snapshot).
not_readable: The body text of the articles (paywalled; worldin.economist.com edition-2018 pages not read).

entries.quote: In America, the Democrats could triumph in a close contest for the House of Representatives, opening the way for the possible impeachment of Donald Trump .
entries.subject: US midterm elections 2018 (House)

entries.quote: Russia will stage the FIFA World Cup at a sensitive time in the country's relations with the West and shortly after an election that will give Vladimir Putin another term as president.
entries.subject: Russian presidential election 2018

entries.quote: Japan's Emperor Akihito prepares to bow out, Cuba's President Raúl Castro steps down, Saudi's King Salman may abdicate.
entries.subject: Leadership changes in Japan, Cuba and Saudi Arabia
entries.note: Akihito abdicated 2019-04-30 (announced for then); the Salman clause is hedged ("may").

entries.quote: But many leaders who have overstayed their welcome (such as Nicolás Maduro in Venezuela ) will try to cling to office.
entries.subject: Maduro stays in office

entries.quote: the chances of a no-deal Brexit are high.
entries.subject: No-deal Brexit
entries.note: Refers to the March 2019 departure date.

entries.quote: Bhutan is forecast to top the league in economic growth; China could overtake Italy to be number one in terms of UNESCO-listed world-heritage sites; and India plans to complete the world's tallest statue
entries.subject: Fastest-growing economy; world heritage sites; tallest statue

entries.quote: sport utility vehicles and their close cousins overtaking all other types in sales of new vehicles
entries.subject: SUVs largest share of new-vehicle sales

entries.quote: the rise of private space ventures reflected most dramatically in SpaceX's plan to send tourists around the Moon
entries.subject: SpaceX lunar tourist flight
entries.note: Describes a plan, not a firm prediction.

entries.quote: The most important landmark will be the approval of the world's first RNA interference drug, heralding the arrival of a new class of drug.
entries.subject: First RNAi drug approval

entries.quote: With luck, too, an old era will end, with the final eradication of polio.
entries.subject: Polio eradication

entries.quote: the world economy tends to tip into a recession every eight to ten years, and the last one ended in 2009.
entries.subject: Global recession timing
entries.note: Context for the statement that 2018 "may in fact be approaching the end" of the recovery; no firm date.

entries.quote: India will be the fastest-growing big economy. China will not be far behind.
entries.subject: Fastest-growing big economy

entries.quote: But it would be a surprise if the presidential election scheduled to take place in Venezuela is allowed to threaten the position of the country’s dictator, Nicolás Maduro.
entries.subject: Venezuelan presidential election 2018

entries.quote: In 2018 his brother Raúl will retire as president.
entries.subject: Raúl Castro retires as Cuban president

entries.quote: Or else they might head to Canada or California, both of which will legalise recreational marijuana.
entries.subject: Recreational cannabis legal in Canada and California

entries.quote: Mary Poppins will return to screens at the end of 2018
entries.subject: Mary Poppins Returns release

notes: Edition number 32 per the press release, which fits a first edition in 1987.
